label: ECM
rationale: obs[S1]: ECM 1073, recorded December 1975 at Tonstudio Bauer, Ludwigsburg; produced by Manfred Eicher; Metheny's first studio recording as leader. obs[S2]: Wikipedia confirms recording December 1975, release 1976; personnel Pat Metheny, Jaco Pastorius, Bob Moses; engineer Martin Wieland. obs[S3]: AllMusic lists styles Post-Bop / Contemporary Jazz / Fusion / Guitar Jazz, recording date December 1975 at Bauer/Tonstudio Bauer Ludwigsburg. obs[S4]: Discogs release 9205620 confirms engineer Martin Wieland, producer Manfred Eicher, and personnel. obs[S5]: MusicBrainz release b60d1bc5-a18c-38ca-a26b-6e040d5d7acb confirms engineer Martin Wieland and producer Manfred Eicher. inf: Landmark modern-jazz guitar debut bridging post-bop melody with electric rhythm; the continuity with the 1960s post-bop and Ornette Coleman lineage is clear, but the fusion tag is present and must be flagged.
continuity_case: Metheny's debut is a song-form, post-bop guitar trio record (including an Ornette Coleman cover) that reaches the 1960s modal/post-bop lineage forward; the electric bass and guitar give it a fusion flavor, but the core argument is melodic improvisation and trio interplay, which I would make if the record had appeared on Milestone or ECM.
scope_flag: ECM gate — 1976 (recorded December 1975), inside window; post-bop/fusion border case — electric instrumentation and the fusion tag are the strongest case against; continuity rests on song-form, post-bop lineage, and the Ornette Coleman connection.

scope_check.boundary_note: Recorded December 1975 and released 1976, it is inside the 1973–1979 band and ECM’s permitted 1969–1979 range, but requires a continuity ruling at both the ECM/modal and fusion boundaries: electric guitar and Jaco Pastorius’s electric bass make the bridge test central.

ballot.case_for: Metheny’s first leader date is a landmark modern-jazz guitar statement and a consequential meeting of Metheny, Pastorius, and Bob Moses; its compact trio interplay has substantial session gravity. The dossier documents a program of Metheny originals plus Ornette Coleman’s "Round Trip / Broadway Blues" (S1), making a concrete link to the 1960s post-bop/avant-garde lineage rather than merely applying a jazz label to electric music. Its melodic writing, improvisational focus, and non-rock rhythmic organization support the case that it extends post-bop practice into the ECM era.
ballot.case_against: The dossier’s sources securely establish credits, dates, and broad style labels, but provide little independent evidence for the larger claims of canonical consensus, influence, or defining-statement status; ECM and discographic documentation cannot by itself prove those claims. The record’s electric guitar-and-bass sound can also be heard as an early foundation for Metheny’s distinct contemporary-jazz/Americana vocabulary, a new late-1970s direction rather than a direct continuation of the modal/post-bop center of this canon. Under the rubric’s anti-drift rule, its fusion-adjacent instrumentation and polished sound are a meaningful scope concern even without a rock backbeat.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes that John treat Bright Size Life as a strong scope call and decide whether its post-bop trio language outweighs its ECM-era fusion/contemporary-jazz departure.
